title: SRS Review AI — wire contract
description: Single source of truth for the JSON exchanged between the Flutter app and the FastAPI proxy. Both sides are tested against contracts/fixtures/*.json. Bump x-contract-version on any breaking change and update both sides in the same PR.

IssueType.description: Quality issue vocabulary for the LLM (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 flavoured). Deterministic rule checks use $defs/CheckId instead — do not mix the two vocabularies. This is the defect CLASS, not the criterion the model was judging: an editable criterion is an id from the criteria list and travels in Issue.criterion_id. `other` is the vocabulary's escape hatch — the server maps any unrecognised value to it rather than failing the unit, because the app rejects an unknown type loudly and a verified finding must not die over a label.

Verification.description: Result of server-side quote verification. 'rejected' issues are DROPPED by the server and never reach the app, so the app only ever sees exact|fuzzy|reordered. 1.1.0 adds 'reordered' — same content as the source but lost order (a PDF table row read cell-by-cell): word coverage is high while no ordered window matches, the tier the 2026-09-28 citation crosscheck asked for. It is a breaking addition: an app speaking 1.0.0 rejects the value loudly rather than rendering a tier it cannot name.

DecisionStatus.description: The closed set of decisions a teacher may record on a submission (ADR-0016 decision 2, ADR-0017). A decision appends to the current round and never overwrites it, so the vocabulary is a closed set written down in one place: the next status someone needs is an ADR amendment, not a string edit. 'rejected' and 'needsRevision' are NOT members — they are document states, not decisions the server records. Added in 1.2.0; the mock web-ui carries the same three-value event vocabulary.

CommentAuthor.description: Who wrote one turn in a round's thread (ADR-0019). Two, and only two, because the two sides hold DIFFERENT credentials: a teacher is authorised by the containing class's write key, a student by possession of the submission id itself. Neither may borrow the other's, and the app token — a shared secret every client holds — authorises neither. Added in 1.3.0.

Comment.description: One turn in the teacher <-> student thread on a submission (ADR-0019). The thread lives on the SUBMISSION, not per revision, so a remark survives a resubmit; `revision` records which round the remark was written against, so the information is not lost by not forking the thread. Append-only: resolving sets `resolved_at` and keeps `body`, and nothing in the API deletes a comment. Replies are a FLAT list under their parent (`replies`), never a tree — a two-person thread does not need arbitrary nesting. `reply_to` is absent on top-level comments, which is how the two shapes stay distinguishable without a second type. Added in 1.3.0.

id.description: Capability id of this one comment or reply (128 bits, like a submission id). It addresses the comment for reply and resolve; it is not a secret, because writing already requires a credential the caller must hold.

body.description: The remark itself. Whitespace-only is rejected; the 2000-character cap is enforced at both ends so the two never disagree about where the edge is.

revision.description: The submission revision this turn was written against. Preserved on purpose: a teacher reading revision 3 can still see which remarks were about revision 1.

at.description: Server clock, second precision, `Z` suffix — the same `_now()` shape as every other timestamp on the wire.

resolvedAt.description: Set when the teacher closes the remark, null while open. Teacher authority only: the group may not close a remark about its own work. Un-resolving clears it back to null and is NOT a delete — a thread that could only ever close would make people write a fresh comment instead of reopening the old one.

replyTo.description: Id of the parent comment. Present on replies under `replies`; omitted entirely on a top-level comment, which is what makes the two shapes distinguishable.

replies.description: Replies to this comment, oldest first. Flat and one level deep by construction. Absent until the first reply.

CheckId.description: Deterministic (rule-based, offline, zero-token) checks derived from the SEP490 syllabus and from review-rules/RULEBOOK.md. M2 reference checks (duplicate_ids, missing_postcondition) extend the same enum — they share the on-wire shape but live in a separate UI section. This list had drifted behind the Dart CheckId enum; it is now complete as of rubric v3, and adding a CheckId without adding it here is the drift to watch for.

criterion_id.description: Id of the evaluation criterion this issue answers, when the model named one — a row from the (editable) criteria list the prompt carried. This is what makes an edited or user-added criterion traceable in the findings; null when the model named none. Additive: an older reader ignores it.

quote.description: Verbatim excerpt from the requirement text. Verified server-side before being returned.

similarity.description: Fuzzy-match ratio; null when verification == exact. Set for 'reordered' too (the best ordered window, below the fuzzy floor).

coverage.description: Word coverage of the quote in the source, order ignored; only set when verification == 'reordered'. Additive in 1.1.0: an older reader ignores it.

context_note.description: Free-text observation about diagrams/images on the requirement's page. NEVER contributes to score (research 10, Risks).

dropped_issue_count.description: Issues the LLM produced whose quote failed verification and were dropped. Surfaced in the UI as the anti-hallucination metric.

prompt_tokens.description: Tokens consumed by the prompt in upstream LLM call.

BatchUnitResult.description: One unit's outcome inside a /review/batch response, addressed by its index in the request's `units` array. Position in the array is NOT the contract: a unit that fails drops out of `results` and lands in `failed`, so a client that zipped by position would attribute scores to the wrong requirement.

BatchUnitFailure.description: A unit the server could not review. The message is provider-neutral (the proxy never forwards a raw provider error) and is shown to the user.

BatchReviewResponse.description: Answer to POST /review/batch. Always 200 when the request itself was acceptable: the units that WERE reviewed are cached and already paid for, so a 502 would make the client throw them away. Batching is a cost optimisation only — every quote in every result is still verified against that unit's own text.

grounded.description: false => the answer was not supported by the document; the app shows the 'not found in document' state (AC5).

DeterministicFinding.description: Produced client-side (Dart) — no network, no tokens. See docs/rubric.md F7/F8/F9.

subject.description: Which UC/requirement the finding is about; null for document-level findings such as uc_count.
